text:
samir: heads up — we've got 3 customer escalations in the last 2 hours after the openapi regen landed in main. symptoms: intermittent 401s from TS/Go clients, Python client shows duplicate retries and a big token billing bump. repro attached below.

mira: sorry — can you paste the failing request/response and the client versions?

samir: minimal repro (curl + generated clients):
```bash
# curl that succeeds with prod bearer
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"prompt":"hello"}' https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate
# same call using ts client (v1.14.0-regenerated) -> 401 sometimes
```
Response snippets:
```
HTTP/2 401
content-type: application/json
{
  "error": {"message": "invalid auth header"}
}
```

dan: interesting — are tokens rotated? or did regen change header name? last regen note mentioned optional `x-project` header becoming required in schema but SDKs defaulted to omitting it.

alex: I saw the CI regen diff — the OpenAPI change moved `authorization` from `header` to `securityScheme` in a few endpoints (spec patch 2026-03-08). The codegen introduced a new header wrapper in TypeScript causing double-encoding of bearer (e.g. `Bearer Bearer ...`) which the auth service rejects with 401. Go client had a retry middleware that treats 401 as retryable due to a bug — hence duplicate requests and billing spike.

support-ops: customer ticket IDs: #C-3789, #C-3790, #C-3791. One customer included logs showing back-to-back requests within 200ms for the same user. They saw 2x tokens billed.

mira: ok actionable list: 1) add quick fix to roll back TS/Go clients on CDN (patch CI artifact) 2) hotfix auth middleware to avoid retrying 401s 3) add integration test to CI to catch double-bearer and retry loops.

samir: I tried bisecting — the last good regen was at pipeline 2201199000. The failing commit is 2201221000 (openapi bump). Patch suggestion: in TS client replace:
```ts
headers['authorization'] = `Bearer ${credentials}`
// -> ensure header value isn't already prefixed
if (!/^Bearer\s+/i.test(headers['authorization'])) {
  headers['authorization'] = `Bearer ${credentials}`
}
```
And in Go client, change retry policy: 401 should be treated as terminal unless response contains `www-authenticate: stale` or explicit `retry-after`.

infra-bot: deploy status: registry:clients-ts v1.14.1-patch rolling -> 3/5 nodes, can promote to all after green smoke tests.

dan: for regression prevention, we should add a small contract test in regen pipeline that:
- generates clients from spec
- runs a tiny auth handshake using a fake token validator (local stub)
- asserts header equals `Bearer <token>` exactly once

mira: also add a lint rule in codegen templates: never autoprefix bearer if header value already looks prefixed.

alex: i've opened a PR with the TS fix + test: https://git.redwood/clients/ts/pull/1824 — contains unit + regen snapshot. Go fix is in draft: https://git.redwood/clients/go/pull/814.

support-ops: customers want ETA and rollback if needed. can we get rollout + rollback playbook?

samir: rollout plan: promote clients-ts patch -> wait 10m smoke, watch metrics (token usage + 429/401 rate) -> if >30% improvement, promote go patch. rollback via CDN tag revert. I'll coordinate with support.

mira: follow-up: add a checklist to regen PR template: verify header mapping, retry-policy audit, and changelog note for auth-related schema changes. Saves future churn.

dan: logging note: add a counter for "client-auth-header-normalization" so we can see how many requests were auto-normalized. makes investigating billing spikes easier.

samir: thanks all. I'll post updates here as we promote the patch. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: smoke tests passed on clients-ts v1.14.1-patch (3/3) — monitoring for 30m.

samir: 30m in — token billing for the affected customers down ~55%, 401s essentially gone. promoting full rollout now.

support-ops: let customers know we've promoted fix + details on why (openapi regen changed header shape, codegen didn't defensively handle pre-prefixed values). include mitigation steps: pin client version or enable CDN tag rollback.

mira: adding postmortem checklist to regen docs and opening a small RFC on regen CI contract testing.

samir: closing loop — thanks team.
